name: Incline Dumbbell Press
cues: Set the bench to about 30 degrees
Keep your shoulder blades tucked into the bench
Lower the dumbbells to the sides of your upper chest
Press up and slightly inward without clanking the weights

qa.note: Family review 2026-10-01 rated minor. review: The dumbbells stop level with the upper chest and converge over the shoulders without touching. With elbowFlare 40 plus the forearm hold, the forearm lean went from 24-38 deg to 16 deg at most. It is the same mid-palm grip-site depth as 101: 148 deg of elbow flexion at the bottom, with the elbows well below the back pad in the side view. | repaired: see repair report | skeptic after repair: This one reads well. The dumbbells stop level with the upper chest (9.9 cm above the sternum site), converge over the shoulders at lockout, and the 3D forearm lean holds at about 20 deg (max 22.7) from mid-descent through the touch. The upper arm stays at least 43.8 deg from the trunk, and the hero view (figure-102.png) reads as a clean incline DB press with the highlight on the chest. What is left: the elbows fold to 145 deg of flexion at the bottom and sit 18.7 cm below the shoulder (the shared grip-site depth). The lean at the touch is about 15 deg frontal (hands inside the elbows) plus 13 sagittal, so the forearms are not truly vertical. The handle path also bulges about 4 cm wider mid-descent (x 0.36 m at f39-f48) than at the bottom (0.32 m). | skeptic after repair: This is the strongest of the six. Forearms stack under the dumbbells through the press in the side view (refute-r2-side/figure-102-side.png, t=0.375 to 0.75) and in the front view (refute-r2-front/figure-102-front.png, t=0.5 and 0.625, hands within about 10 px of the elbows). The dumbbells converge at the top with a clear gap, consistent with 'without clanking'. Hands are closed on the handles (refute-r2-hands/figure-102-wrist_R.png) and the feet are flat and still. It is not ok because of the shared elbow fold: in the side view at t=0.5 and 0.625 the elbow sits at or below the back-pad edge and the arm is folded far past 100 deg of flexion (the repair measured 148 deg), outside the research band.
